title: Integrated Policy: Budgeting & Forecasting, Contracts, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition (RevRec & Billing)
author: Samantha Ortiz
content:
Purpose

This integrated policy defines Redwood Inference’s standardized processes and control points for: budgeting and forecasting, contracts and legal approvals, procurement and purchasing, and revenue recognition & billing. The goal is to:

- Ensure consistent, audit-ready financial controls across pre-commit (budgeting) and post-commit (procurement, contracting) activities.
- Reduce cycle time for commonly repeated transactions while enforcing segregation of duties for material commitments.
- Maintain ASC 606–aligned revenue recognition rules and high accuracy in customer billing.

Scope

Applies to all Redwood Inc. business units and legal entities where Redwood Inference owns the budget and contracting authority. This includes hosted API sales, Dedicated contracts, Private deployments, professional services, and platform add-ons. Exemptions must be approved by Finance and Legal.

Definitions (key terms)

- Budget Owner: individual accountable for annual budget line(s) and monthly forecast updates. Typically Product, Engineering, or GTM leads.
- Purchase Order (PO): formal procurement commitment issued via ProcureFlow (our procurement system).
- Committed Contract: Signed agreement with monetary commitments and/or SLAs.
- Revenue Event: Executable trigger for revenue recognition (customer acceptance, usage record, or invoice issuance).
- RevRec System: NetSuite (general ledger + RevRec subledger) integrated with BillingEngine and UsageIngest.

1) Budgeting & Forecasting (Policy + Controls)

Overview

Annual and rolling forecasts are the primary controls for spend and capacity planning. Budgets are set annually and reforecasted monthly (rolling 12 months). Forecast accuracy targets and responsibilities are described below.

Roles & Ownership

- Finance: owns consolidation, policy, and reporting; performs variance analysis.
- Budget Owners: provide bottoms-up budgets and monthly forecast updates.
- FP&A Manager: coordinates planning cadence and publishes consolidated forecast.

Cadence & Deliverables

1. Annual planning (Oct–Dec): Budget owners submit FY+1 budgets using BudgetKit template. FP&A consolidates and presents to Exec for approval by Dec 15.
2. Monthly reforecast: Budget owners update forecast by the 5th business day; FP&A publishes consolidated forecast by the 10th.
3. Quarterly re-forecast deep-dive: cross-functional review of major variances (>10% or >$250k).

Targets & KPIs

- Forecast accuracy target: Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) <= 8% for operating expenses and <= 5% for revenue.
- Budget variance threshold for escalation: Variances > 10% and > $250k require a remediation plan.

Approvals & Controls

- Any non-discretionary cost not in budget requires an escalation to the FP&A Manager and written approval from the CFO for amounts > $250k.
- Capital expenditures (CapEx) follow the CapEx approval matrix (see section Table: Approval Matrix).

Table: Approval Matrix (text)

- <= $5,000: Budget owner approval; via ProcureFlow requisition.
- $5,001–$50,000: Budget owner + Finance Manager approval.
- $50,001–$250,000: Budget owner + Finance Manager + Head of Department (HoD).
- > $250,000: CFO + Legal review + Procurement Director (mandatory contract review).

2) Contracts & Legal Process

Overview

All material agreements must be routed through the Legal Contract Intake system and use approved contract templates unless Legal approves deviations. The Contract Intake ticket must include: proposed terms, commercial summary, risk flags, and desired effective date.

Templates & Standard Clauses

- Standard Customer Master Agreement (CMA) for hosted API and Dedicated offerings.
- Professional Services SOW template with acceptance criteria and milestone-based billing.
- NDAs, reseller agreements, and MSP addendums maintained in the Legal Template library.

Redlined Approval Workflow

1. Sales/Prod/Eng creates Contract Intake ticket with draft and commercial summary.
2. Legal performs contract review within Service Level Times (SLTs):
   - Standard template, no redlines: 2 business days.
   - Moderate redlines (commercial terms changed): 5 business days.
   - Complex/enterprise negotiations: target 10–15 business days (depends on risk).
3. If contract value > $250k or includes data residency/Security exceptions: Legal + Security + SOC/Compliance must approve.
4. Signature authority:
   - Up to $250k: VP Sales (or delegated).
   - $250k–$1M: Head of GTM + CFO.
   - >$1M: CEO (or CFO with exec delegation) and in all cases Legal sign-off.

Contractual SLRs & Financial Terms (examples)

- Payment terms: Net 30 standard for enterprise customers; Net 45 by exception with CFO approval.
- Refunds & credits: governed by SOW acceptance and Customer Success signoff. Credits for outages follow SLA credit schedule embedded in CSA.
- Term & auto-renewal: default 12-month term with 30-day renewal notice unless negotiated.

3) Procurement Procedures (Operational Steps)

Overview

ProcureFlow is the company procurement system. All purchases that require a vendor commitment must flow through ProcureFlow and generate a Purchase Order (PO) prior to work being performed or goods being delivered, except where corporate card policy or petty cash exceptions apply.

Vendor Onboarding Requirements

- Completed vendor profile in ProcureFlow, including W-9/Entity docs, primary contact, and payment remit info.
- Security & privacy questionnaire for vendors with access to sensitive data (Security will classify vendors as Low/Medium/High risk).
- Finance runs GL coding and tax classification during PO creation.

Procurement Steps (numbered)

1. Requisition created by Budget Owner in ProcureFlow with business justification and desired vendor.
2. Obtain competitive bids for purchases > $25,000 (minimum 2 bids). Document comparison in requisition.
3. Procurement reviews and issues a PO. PO must reference contract number if a Committed Contract exists.
4. Vendor invoicing: invoices must reference PO number and be sent to AP@redwood.com or via EDI/API to BillingEngine.
5. Goods receipt / service acceptance: requestor confirms receipt in ProcureFlow to trigger three-way match and payment.

Escalation & Exceptions

- Emergency purchases (e.g., replace failed capacity affecting customer SLAs) can be executed via Emergency ProcureFlow channel but must be ratified with a retroactive PO within 5 business days.
- Corporate card usage limited to <= $5,000 with monthly reconciliation and receipts uploaded to ProcureFlow.

4) Revenue Recognition (RevRec) and Billing Policy

Principles

Revenue recognition follows ASC 606 principles: identify contract(s) with customer, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to obligations, and recognize revenue when (or as) performance obligations are satisfied. Our RevRec implementation uses NetSuite RevRec integrated with BillingEngine (usage records from UsageIngest) and manual adjustments where required.

Common Revenue Scenarios

- Hosted API (Usage-based):
  - Performance obligation: delivery of API access and token processing.
  - Recognition: As usage occurs (over time) based on daily usage records. Billing cycles monthly.
  - Deferred revenue: initial prepayments or committed monthly minimums recognized ratably over the service period.

- Dedicated / Reserved Capacity (Subscription + Commitment):
  - Performance obligation: reservation of capacity and priority access.
  - Recognition: ratably over the contract term (monthly). Any implementation services are recognized on completion of acceptance criteria in SOW.

- Professional Services / Implementation:
  - Performance obligation: deliverables (milestones) with customer acceptance.
  - Recognition: milestone completion (point in time) or over time for long-lived engagements with input method.

Billing & Invoicing Rules

- Billing cadence: Monthly in arrears for usage; Monthly in advance for committed subscriptions unless otherwise negotiated.
- Invoice content: contract number, PO (if provided), usage summary (if applicable), tax details, payment terms, and remittance instructions.
- Billing disputes: customer must notify billing@redwood.com within 45 days of invoice date to qualify for dispute handling. Billing disputes are routed to Revenue Operations for triage; adjustments posted within 30 days of validated dispute.

Tax & International Considerations

- Finance owns tax determination and ensures correct VAT/GST handling for cross-border customers. Pricing team must supply country of sale at contract intake.

Revenue Cutover & Month-end Close

- Usage ingestion cutoff: 2 business days after month-end to allow for late usage corrections. Adjustments after cutoff are treated as subsequent period adjustments unless approved by Accounting.
- Month-end checklist (selected):
  - All signed contracts uploaded to Contract Repository.
  - Revenue schedules generated by RevRec run and reviewed by Revenue Operations.
  - Deferred revenue roll-forward prepared and reviewed by Accounting.

5) Controls, Audit, and Compliance

Segregation of Duties

- Requisitioning, approval, and payment are separated: Requestor != Approver != AP Payment Approver.
- Contract negotiation party must not be the payment approver for the same vendor.

Audit & Documentation

- All POs, invoices, contracts and change orders must be stored in the Contract Repository and ProcureFlow. Records retention follows the Records Retention Policy (7 years for material contracts and tax-related documents).
- Internal audit will perform an annual control assessment on procurement, contract approvals, and RevRec processes.

Key Controls & Monitoring

- Monthly Finance report: PO to invoice match rate (target > 98%), late invoice resolution time (< 15 days), and billing dispute backlog (< 5 open older than 30 days).
- RevRec health checks: daily automated alerts for revenue recognition exceptions (mismatch between BillingEngine and RevRec) with SLA to resolve within 3 business days.

6) Operational Playbooks & Quick Procedures

A. Creating a Contract Intake Ticket (quick steps)
1. Navigate to Contract Intake portal.
2. Upload proposed contract or select template.
3. Enter commercial summary, estimated ARR/TCV, requested signatory, and any security/data exceptions.
4. Select Legal review priority (standard/moderate/expedite) and submit.

B. Raising a Procurement Requisition (quick steps)
1. Login to ProcureFlow; create new requisition.
2. Attach vendor quote(s), W-9, and GL code.
3. Select approver per the approval matrix and submit.

C. Revenue recognition exception triage (quick steps)
1. Revenue Operations receives RevRec alert.
2. Validate usage files and contract terms.
3. If misallocation, create journal entry request with supporting docs and route to Accounting for approval.

7) Responsibilities & Contact Points

- Finance (Accounting & RevOps): accounting@redwood.com (month-end, RevRec questions).
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.com (vendor onboarding, PO issuance).
- Legal: contracts@redwood.com (contract intake and templates).
- Billing & Revenue Ops: billing@redwood.com (invoices, disputes, usage ingestion).

References & Related Documents

- Finance: Budgeting Playbook 2026 (link: /confluence/finance-and-legal/budgeting-and-forecasting/finance-legal-integrated-budgeting-procurement-revrec-playbook-2026.json)
- Legal: Contract Template Library (link: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/contract-template-library)
- Systems: ProcureFlow user guide, NetSuite RevRec operations guide, BillingEngine integration spec.

Appendix: Checklist for New Vendor Engagement (text table)

- Vendor profile created in ProcureFlow: Yes/No
- W-9 or local tax docs collected: Yes/No
- Security questionnaire completed (if required): Yes/No
- Contract template used and uploaded to Contract Repository: Yes/No
- PO issued prior to work: Yes/No
- Invoices to reference PO and sent to AP: Yes/No

Change History

- 2026-11-20: Updated to align RevRec cutoff rules with UsageIngest enhancements and to raise forecast cadence expectations.

Approval
